Direct shear test on RSM-a soil at relative density 1.0 to 1.3; apparatus: direct shear (University of Notre Dame); loading: normal stress 4695 psf. Recorded: shear stress and dilation vs shear displacement. One of 5 tests of this soil and density at normal stresses from 35.1 to 224.8 kPa, the family the report used to draw the failure envelope.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 105 of the 129 points, and the rest were settled against the scan. Student reviewers have looked at 15 of the 129 points on the scan; two reviewers confirmed 5 of them (see the provenance page). The test setup is incomplete: specimen height, displacement rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![shear stress and dilation (normal displacement; positive up) against shear displacement, SI units, this test in red and the other tests printed in Fig. C-3C in gray. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-ds-fc-3c-n4695.png){.lightbox}

Peak shear stress 267.0 kPa at 2.42 mm shear displacement; 227.4 kPa at 6.30 mm, the end of the record. Dilation 918 micrometers at the end.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-3c-n4695/observations.csv) (129 points: 25 plotted symbols, 101 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1: shear stress in Pa against shear displacement in m; panel 2: dilation (normal displacement; positive up) in m against shear displacement in m; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-3c-n4695/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 12 micrometers in shear displacement, 1.3 kPa in shear stress (0.5 percent of the peak), 31 micrometers in dilation. Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 105 of the 129 points; the other 24 were settled against the scan (read by one reader and verified by the other, or decided between two readings). [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-fc-3c).
